name: Lysimachus
charge: Sacrilege: robbing the temple with Menelaus' consent
summary: Menelaus' brother committed many sacrileges in the city by his brother's consent and carried away much gold. The multitude gathered against him; he armed three thousand men under a captain of years and madness and attacked the crowd.
offense: Plunder of the sanctuary treated as family business, then armed force against the people who objected. The narrator calls him the church-robber.
judgment: The people took up stones and clubs and ashes, wounded many, killed some, put the rest to flight, and slew Lysimachus himself beside the treasury. Judgment executed by the congregation at the scene of the crime.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not steal another's property.
Priests are to keep the charge of the sanctuary and tabernacle of the congregation and keep it supplied and in proper order.
God executes judgment here on the earth.
The congregation of the people (jury) can judge matters in a criminal case.

text.text: Now when many sacrileges had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the fruit thereof was spread abroad, the multitude gathered themselves together against Lysimachus, many vessels of gold being already carried away.

Whereupon the common people rising, and being filled with rage, Lysimachus armed about three thousand men, and began first to offer violence; one Auranus being the leader, a man far gone in years, and no less in folly.

They then seeing the attempt of Lysimachus, some of them caught stones, some clubs, others taking handfuls of dust, that was next at hand, cast them all together upon Lysimachus, and those that set upon them.
Thus many of them they wounded, and some they struck to the ground, and all of them they forced to flee: but as for the churchrobber himself, him they killed beside the treasury.
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.
